title: How important is choosing the right name
titleChinese: 取个好名字到底有多重要？
paragraphs: New parents often spend a long time debating what to call their newborn. Should they name them after a relative, a famous person or just pick a name at random? For many of us it can be quite the gruelling task, but it’s our children who need to live with our choice. So, how important is the name you choose?

Names usually stay with us for a lifetime, unless we decide to change them. They become part of our identity. Quite often we hear stories of celebrities giving their children unusual names, while other people give their children names which have special meanings, for example, the name Sarah comes from a Hebrew word meaning ‘princess’. Sadly, though, our parents don’t always get it right.

So, what if you don’t like your given name? A study led by psychologist Jean Twenge found that a person who hates the moniker given to them is more likely to have greater psychological adjustment issues – possibly due to low self-esteem. This is because our title becomes a symbol of our self, and if we loathe our name, our confidence may be affected.

And what if your name is no longer popular? While names like Ethel and Gladys were once in fashion, they now sound a bit out of date, which can be embarrassing. And when it comes to unpopular names which aren’t trending, they may even affect our love lives. Studies have shown that people with old-fashioned names are more likely to be rejected on dating apps.

However, if you choose an unusual name, it’s not all bad news. According to a study conducted by Professor David Zhu, people with uncommon names can develop a sense of uniqueness and can often become more creative and open-minded.

So, when choosing your offspring’s name, there are a fair few things to consider – but going for something too common or too old-fashioned may not be a great choice. And, if your children hate your choice, they can always select a nickname.

vocabulary.entry: newborn /ˈnjuːbɔːn/ n. 新生儿
vocabulary.example: The nurse gently placed the newborn in its mother's arms.
vocabulary.translation: 护士小心翼翼地把新生儿放到妈妈怀里。

vocabulary.entry: random /ˈrændəm/ adj. 随机的；随意的
vocabulary.example: The winner will be chosen at random from all the participants.
vocabulary.translation: 获胜者将从所有参与者中随机选出。

vocabulary.entry: gruelling /ˈɡruːəlɪŋ/ adj. 使人精疲力竭的；费力的
vocabulary.example: The team faced a gruelling schedule of matches in the tournament.
vocabulary.translation: 该队在锦标赛中面临着高强度的赛程。

vocabulary.entry: identity /aɪˈdentəti/ n. 身份；特征
vocabulary.example: He struggled to find his identity after moving to a new country.
vocabulary.translation: 移居异国后，他努力寻找自己的身份定位。

vocabulary.entry: celebrity /səˈlebrəti/ n. 名人；名流
vocabulary.example: The celebrity avoided the paparazzi by leaving through the back door.
vocabulary.translation: 这位名人从后门离开，避开了狗仔队。

vocabulary.entry: Hebrew /ˈhiːbruː/ adj. 希伯来语的；希伯来人的
vocabulary.example: Many ancient religious texts were written in Hebrew.
vocabulary.translation: 许多古老的宗教典籍是用希伯来语写成的。

vocabulary.entry: given name /ˈɡɪvn neɪm/ n. 教名；名字
vocabulary.example: Her given name is Mary, but everyone calls her Molly.
vocabulary.translation: 她的名字是玛丽，但大家都叫她莫莉。

vocabulary.entry: moniker /ˈmɒnɪkə/ n. 名字；绰号
vocabulary.example: The singer is known by the moniker "The Prince of Pop".
vocabulary.translation: 这位歌手被冠以“流行音乐之王”的称号。

vocabulary.entry: psychological /ˌsaɪkəˈlɒdʒɪkl/ adj. 心理的；心理学的
vocabulary.example: The patient is receiving psychological treatment for anxiety.
vocabulary.translation: 这位患者正因焦虑症接受心理治疗。

vocabulary.entry: adjustment /əˈdʒʌstmənt/ n. 调整；适应
vocabulary.example: She needed some time for adjustment to the new job.
vocabulary.translation: 她需要一些时间来适应新工作。

vocabulary.entry: self-esteem /ˌself ɪˈstiːm/ n. 自尊；自尊心
vocabulary.example: Praise from teachers can boost a child's self-esteem.
vocabulary.translation: 老师的表扬能增强孩子的自尊心。

vocabulary.entry: symbol /ˈsɪmbl/ n. 象征；标志
vocabulary.example: The dove is a universal symbol of peace.
vocabulary.translation: 鸽子是公认的和平象征。

vocabulary.entry: loathe /ləʊð/ v. 厌恶；憎恨
vocabulary.example: She loathes the idea of getting up early on weekends.
vocabulary.translation: 她很讨厌周末早起。

vocabulary.entry: confidence /ˈkɒnfɪdəns/ n. 信心；自信
vocabulary.example: Regular practice will help you build confidence in public speaking.
vocabulary.translation: 经常练习会帮你建立公开演讲的信心。

vocabulary.entry: out of date /ˌaʊt əv ˈdeɪt/ adj. 过时的；陈旧的
vocabulary.example: These fashion trends are already out of date this year.
vocabulary.translation: 这些流行趋势今年已经过时了。

vocabulary.entry: embarrassing /ɪmˈbærəsɪŋ/ adj. 令人尴尬的；使人难堪的
vocabulary.example: It was an embarrassing moment when she forgot her lines on stage.
vocabulary.translation: 她在舞台上忘词的那一刻，真是尴尬极了。

vocabulary.entry: trending /ˈtrendɪŋ/ adj. 流行的；热门的
vocabulary.example: This song is currently trending on social media platforms.
vocabulary.translation: 这首歌目前在社交媒体平台上很热门。

vocabulary.entry: reject /rɪˈdʒekt/ v. 拒绝；回绝
vocabulary.example: The university rejected his application due to insufficient qualifications.
vocabulary.translation: 由于资历不足，这所大学拒绝了他的申请。

vocabulary.entry: uncommon /ʌnˈkɒmən/ adj. 不寻常的；罕见的
vocabulary.example: It is uncommon to see snow in this region in winter.
vocabulary.translation: 这个地区冬天很少下雪。

vocabulary.entry: uniqueness /juːˈniːknəs/ n. 独特性；唯一性
vocabulary.example: The designer emphasized the uniqueness of each handmade piece.
vocabulary.translation: 这位设计师强调每件手工制品的独特性。

vocabulary.entry: creative /kriˈeɪtɪv/ adj. 创造性的；有创造力的
vocabulary.example: The company encourages its employees to come up with creative ideas.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司鼓励员工提出有创意的想法。

vocabulary.entry: open-minded /ˌəʊpən ˈmaɪndɪd/ adj. 思想开明的；无偏见的
vocabulary.example: We need an open-minded approach to solving this problem.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要用开明的态度来解决这个问题。

vocabulary.entry: offspring /ˈɒfsprɪŋ/ n. 子女；后代
vocabulary.example: The bird feeds its offspring with insects it has caught.
vocabulary.translation: 这只鸟用捕捉到的昆虫喂养幼鸟。

vocabulary.entry: fair /feə/ adj. 相当多的；不少的
vocabulary.example: There are a fair number of books on this subject in the library.
vocabulary.translation: 图书馆里有不少关于这个主题的书籍。

vocabulary.entry: nickname /ˈnɪkneɪm/ n. 昵称；外号
vocabulary.example: His friends gave him the nickname "Tiny" because he was very tall.
vocabulary.translation: 因为他个子很高，朋友们给他取了个外号叫“小不点”。

sentences.english: New parents often spend a long time debating what to call their newborn.
sentences.chinese: 新手父母常常会花很长时间纠结该给新生儿取什么名字。

sentences.chinese: 是用亲戚的名字给孩子命名，还是效仿名人，又或者只是随机选一个？

sentences.english: For many of us it can be quite the gruelling task, but it’s our children who need to live with our choice.
sentences.chinese: 对很多人来说，这是一项相当费力的任务，但最终要一辈子使用这个名字的，却是我们的孩子。

sentences.english: So, how important is the name you choose?
sentences.chinese: 那么，取名这件事到底有多重要呢？

sentences.english: Names usually stay with us for a lifetime, unless we decide to change them.
sentences.chinese: 名字通常会伴随我们一生，除非我们决定改名。

sentences.english: They become part of our identity.
sentences.chinese: 它会成为我们身份的一部分。

sentences.english: Quite often we hear stories of celebrities giving their children unusual names, while other people give their children names which have special meanings, for example, the name Sarah comes from a Hebrew word meaning ‘princess’.
sentences.chinese: 我们经常会看到名人给孩子取独特名字的新闻，而普通人给孩子取名时，往往会选择带有特殊寓意的名字。比如，“萨拉”这个名字源自希伯来语，意思是“公主”。

sentences.english: Sadly, though, our parents don’t always get it right.
sentences.chinese: 但遗憾的是，父母有时候取的名字并不理想。

sentences.english: So, what if you don’t like your given name?
sentences.chinese: 如果你不喜欢父母给你取的名字，会怎么样呢？

sentences.english: A study led by psychologist Jean Twenge found that a person who hates the moniker given to them is more likely to have greater psychological adjustment issues – possibly due to low self-esteem.
sentences.chinese: 心理学家琼·特文奇主导的一项研究发现，厌恶自己本名的人，更容易出现心理适应问题，这可能与自卑心理有关。

sentences.english: This is because our title becomes a symbol of our self, and if we loathe our name, our confidence may be affected.
sentences.chinese: 因为名字会成为我们自我认知的象征，如果我们讨厌自己的名字，自信心也可能会受到影响。

sentences.english: And what if your name is no longer popular?
sentences.chinese: 要是你的名字已经不再流行了，又会如何？

sentences.english: While names like Ethel and Gladys were once in fashion, they now sound a bit out of date, which can be embarrassing.
sentences.chinese: 像“埃塞尔”“格拉迪斯”这类名字，曾经风靡一时，但如今听上去已经有些过时，这可能会让人感到尴尬。

sentences.english: And when it comes to unpopular names which aren’t trending, they may even affect our love lives.
sentences.chinese: 而且，一个不够时髦、不受欢迎的名字，甚至可能影响我们的感情生活。

sentences.english: Studies have shown that people with old-fashioned names are more likely to be rejected on dating apps.
sentences.chinese: 研究表明，名字比较老派的人，在交友软件上被拒绝的概率更高。

sentences.english: However, if you choose an unusual name, it’s not all bad news.
sentences.chinese: 不过，如果给孩子取一个特别的名字，也并非全是坏处。

sentences.english: According to a study conducted by Professor David Zhu, people with uncommon names can develop a sense of uniqueness and can often become more creative and open-minded.
sentences.chinese: 大卫·朱教授的研究显示，名字独特的人，会逐渐培养出一种独特的自我意识，而且往往会更具创造力，思想也更开明。

sentences.english: So, when choosing your offspring’s name, there are a fair few things to consider – but going for something too common or too old-fashioned may not be a great choice.
sentences.chinese: 因此，给孩子取名时，确实有不少事情需要考虑。名字太过普通或者太过老派，都未必是好选择。

sentences.english: And, if your children hate your choice, they can always select a nickname.
sentences.chinese: 当然，如果孩子不喜欢你取的名字，他们也完全可以给自己改名。
